transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Vale (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Head of ML, Eversource), Tom Reynolds (Infra), Alex Gomez (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): final runbook items, telemetry gating, dry-run scheduling
Topics (auto): canary thresholds, A/B routing, rollback steps, telemetry hooks, RBAC/KMS notes

[00:00] Lina (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda update — runbook walkthrough, canary thresholds, ab routing matrix, and dry run timing. priya, you want to kick off with any constraints since last week?

[00:22] Priya (Eversource): yep thanks lina. short thing — compliance asked that we keep logs for 14 months now, and KMS key rotation procedures have to be documented in the runbook. also, low tolerance for p50 spikes during peak. so we want clear traffic gates.

[00:45] Tom (Eversource): and to add — our networking team needs the exact VPC egress rules, we can't open things wide for the pilot. staging test has a narrow window tuesday night.

[01:10] Marcus (Redwood SE): ok got it. on the KMS and logs — we can add a section that notes integration with your CMK via the Redwood Private key manager flow, and call out audit log endpoints. rough note: we'll include sample terraform snippets.

[01:35] Alex (Eversource): two high-level asks: 1) simple rollback trigger based on a few telemetry signals, 2) an A/B split that lets us ramp from 5% to 50% in two steps.

[01:58] Lina: perfect. for rollback triggers we typically use a combination: 1) 5-minute error rate delta > 2x baseline, 2) p95 latency increase above threshold, 3) quality regression on the eval set — we can wire in your eval queries to the quality monitor.

[02:25] Priya: on the evals, can we set a blind set of prompts that we run every 10 minutes during the canary? not sure cost wise but it helps.

[02:49] Marcus: yes, we support scheduled eval probes. cost impact will be small if we keep the probes brief — maybe 25 short prompts. we'll include a suggestion in the runbook with expected token cost estimates.

[03:12] Tom: networking question — during rollback, do you need to change routing at our edge or can Redwood do a model level fallback?

[03:30] Marcus: good question. we have two options: route-level traffic steering (you change the LB weights) or runtime fallback where requests hit Redwood control plane and we redirect to a compatible cheaper variant. for fastest rollback we recommend LB weight flip from your side; for automatic graceful degradation we can do runtime fallback but it adds a call path.

[03:55] Priya: sounds like we prefer LB weight flip for the initial canary, then explore runtime fallback for dedicated later.

[04:12] Lina: noted. the runbook will have both methods documented with pros/cons. next — canary thresholds. Marcus, you had a draft?

[04:30] Marcus: yes. recommended steps: start at 5% traffic for 30 minutes. if p95 latency within 1.3x baseline and error rate delta < 1.5x and eval pass rate > 98% then move to 20% for 45 minutes. then 50% for 1 hour. final ramp to 100% only after a green signal and sign-off. we also include abort conditions for each step.

[05:05] Alex: can we shorten the middle step if signals look very healthy? we'd like ability to do accelerated ramp to 50% in 30 minutes.

[05:20] Marcus: yes, we'll include an "accelerated ramp" checklist — must have no degradation on telemetry and one stakeholder sign-off. we'll document who can sign off.

[05:40] Priya: who typically signs off on Redwood side for these?

[05:47] Lina: for the pilot it's me, but for Dedicated/enterprise the CSM or release owner gets a role. we'll list names in the runbook.

[06:01] Tom: alarms — what thresholds do you recommend for auto rollback? p95 > X ms?

[06:12] Marcus: suggested defaults: p95 > baseline * 1.5 OR error rate > 2x baseline OR eval fail rate delta > 3% absolute. we can tune numbers to your baseline after we ingest 48 hours of telemetry.

[06:36] Priya: that 48 hour ingest is important. we won't lock thresholds until we see the pilot baseline.

[06:45] Lina: understood. next — A/B routing. alex, do you want pure A/B for feature comparison or is it for soft rollouts?

[06:58] Alex: primarily feature comparison, some quality side-by-side between model variants. we also want sticky sessions for a subset of users.

[07:15] Marcus: ok. runbook will include an A/B matrix: variants A (current) vs B (new model/quantized) with user segment definitions. sticky session approach: route via cookie or header so we can keep users consistent across sessions. note: sticky sessions complicate garbage collection of prefix caches so we'll document cache warm strategies.

[07:45] Tom: cache warm — we hit cache miss storms in last experiment. any recommendations?

[07:52] Marcus: yes, strategies: 1) pre-warm with a curated set of high-volume prefixes, 2) progressive traffic ramp to avoid cold-start storm, 3) use Redwood's KV cache hints to persist warmed entries between hosts when safe. small caveat: some of the cache persistence requires Dedicated/private mode. we'll flag that.

[08:25] Priya: understood — we might want Dedicated long-term but for pilot we'll stick to hosted. any differences for the runbook between hosted and private?

[08:36] Lina: we will include two paths: hosted (Redwood API) and private (VPC/on-prem). hosted path will show control plane runbook steps; private adds network-specific tasks (firewall rules, KMS integration). we'll mark which steps are required for hosted only.

[08:58] Alex: telemetry — what are the minimal dashboards we need to create before dry-run?

[09:07] Marcus: minimal: p95/p50 latency, token throughput, error rate, eval probe pass rate, CPU/GPU utilization per node (if Dedicated), request distribution, and business-level success metric from your side (we can ingest an API to compute QPS of accepted responses).

[09:32] Priya: do you have a template dashboard we can plug into Datadog?

[09:38] Marcus: yes, I'll attach a Datadog dashboard JSON in the runbook. Lina will share it.

[09:48] Lina: will do. also we'll include recommended alert severities and escalation path.

[10:02] Tom: for the dry-run — can we simulate error conditions? like spike latency or eval failures?

[10:12] Marcus: absolutely. test plan will include induced failures: 1) introduce artificial latency on test traffic, 2) drop a percentage of responses to simulate errors, 3) fake eval set regressions by injecting bad responses. we will script these so you can run them in a controlled way.

[10:40] Alex: timeline question — after dry-run, how long to make changes and re-run?

[10:48] Lina: depends on findings. typical is 1 week to triage and update configs for small issues. for infra-level blockers maybe longer. we'll document expected SLAs for fixes in the runbook.

[11:02] Priya: compliance — we need to validate audit logs after dry-run. do you keep immutable logs?

[11:12] Marcus: we keep event logs and can ship them to your S3 bucket. for immutability we recommend writing to the KMS-encrypted bucket with object lock if you need WORM semantics. we'll add a section.

[11:36] Tom: small nit — can you call out exact API endpoints and expected request/response payloads in the runbook? our infra team needs that for firewall whitelists.

[11:48] Lina: yes API appendix with example curl, headers, and IP ranges.

[12:05] Alex: regarding stakeholders — who from our side should be present during canary to sign off? Priya: you? Tom? anyone else?

[12:15] Priya: I will be primary, Tom for infra, Alex for product, and I want a business owner backup in case I'm not available. we'll call out alternates.

[12:30] Marcus: good. we'll include a sign-off checklist in runbook with names and contact numbers.

[12:45] Lina: rolling back — do we want an automated rollback or manual? seems you prefer manual LB flip. are we good leaving an automated fallback as optional?

[12:58] Alex: manual flip for pilot. optional automatic fallback later.

[13:10] Marcus: noted. for manual flips we'll provide an ops runbook to change weights in your LB (example scripts) plus a verification step to confirm traffic actually moved and caches warmed.

[13:34] Priya: what about data residency in the logs? some customers require EU-only storage. we may have EU users that need EU-only residency.

[13:45] Lina: we'll include residency notes. hosted supports region pinning and logs exported to region-specific buckets. for strict EU-only policies we recommend Private deployment.

[14:02] Tom: can you also include a short section about cost impact during ramp? token cost estimates per step?

[14:13] Marcus: yes, we'll include a cost table using your projected traffic profile — quick estimate for the 5/20/50 steps and probes.

[14:30] Alex: ok good. unusual question — do you have a dry-run checklist for stakeholder comms? like pre-announce, customer support standby?

[14:40] Lina: yes, communications checklist: pre-announce, expected user impact (if any), support rota, rollback contact, a status page update template. we'll add it.

[15:00] Priya: let's talk about measurement of quality — you said eval pass rate will be used, but can we also capture a small human review sample? we can do that after 20% ramp.

[15:18] Marcus: yes, human-in-the-loop sampling after 20% is a good idea. we'll include a quick review UI flow — export samples to your annotation queue.

[15:38] Alex: any gotchas you saw in previous pilots?

[15:44] Marcus: two common ones — misconfigured stickiness causing uneven distribution, and not warming caches before ramping which can create latency spikes. both are addressable with the runbook steps we discussed.

[16:03] Tom: for the staging dry-run on 2026-04-14, do we need credentials changes or are we reusing current tokens?

[16:12] Lina: we recommend new staging API keys and a short-lived token pattern so nothing accidentally hits prod. we'll include token lifecycle steps.

[16:30] Priya: ok. last section — security review. anything new since last week?

[16:37] Marcus: no new items. we will attach the SOC 2 summary and SAML SSO integration guide. also noted KMS integration plan and audit export steps.

[16:55] Alex: great. so recap — runbook sent by monday (Lina), telemetry dashboard + alerts (Marcus), customer provides staging windows and VPC details (Tom), schedule dry-run for 2026-04-14. any objections?

[17:16] Priya: none. sounds good.

[17:23] Tom: none.

[17:28] Lina: i'll send calendar invites for the dry-run and a pre-dry-run checklist meeting 48 hours before.

[17:36] Marcus: i'll prepare the Datadog JSON and the failure injection scripts.

[17:45] Alex: i'll prep a short internal comms for customers and support.

[17:52] Priya: ok. one more quick question — do we want to include a fallback to a cheaper quantized variant during peak to save cost?

[18:05] Marcus: yes that's the runtime fallback path i mentioned; we'll document how to configure quantized variants and the quality tradeoffs. we can also provide a simulation of cost savings per hour at different traffic levels.

[18:28] Priya: perfect. thanks everyone.

[18:33] Lina: thanks all. we'll follow up with the runbook and artifacts.

[18:42] (meeting closes)

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-IDs and ASR artifacts; proper nouns sometimes garbled (eg "K V cache" instead of "KV cache").
